title: Run-to-Stable: Reliability Playbook and Decision Slate
content:
Purpose:
This is a concise, operational playbook to carry new model-serving features from early launch through stable, SLO-backed production. It is intended for cross-functional teams (SRE, serving-runtime, platform, product, solutions engineering, and support) and focuses on decision points, gating criteria, instrumentation, and escalation paths.

Context and problem statement:
- Recent launches have shown variability in latency P95/P99 under real traffic patterns; teams need a repeatable pathway to stabilize services while balancing feature velocity.
- We need clear SLO definitions tied to customer-impacting user journeys, and a practical roadmap to instrument, measure, and act.

Goals (90-day horizon):
1) Define and adopt unified SLOs for model-serving critical paths for two pilot features (chat-streaming, batch-embed).
2) Implement telemetry and alerting for SLO signals + error budgets surfaced in Console dashboards.
3) Run two canary-to-stable rollouts with documented remediation and rollback playbooks.
4) Reduce token-serving P99 tail latency by 20% on pilot services or flag mitigations.

Scope (in-scope / out-of-scope):
- In-scope: SLO design for request latency and successful-response rate, instrumentation of request-level traces and token-level latency histograms, alert routing, canary/A-B rollout plan, runbooks for degradation scenarios.
- Out-of-scope: long-term capacity planning for Dedicated pools, billing model changes, deep kernel-level runtime changes (these will be coordinated but not owned by this project).

Stakeholders and roles:
- Initiative lead: Ava Chen (SRE) — coordinates cross-team cadence and readiness gates.
- Serving-runtime lead: Marcus Li — ensures telemetry hooks and safe fallback variants.
- Platform/Console: Priya Rao — dashboarding and SLO visualization, error budget UI.
- Product (hosted-api): Sofia Alvarez — product acceptance criteria and customer msgs.
- Solutions/CS: Diego Martinez — beta customer coordination and incident playbook testing.
- Escalation path: on-call SRE -> SRE lead -> Platform eng -> Product PM.

Decision checkpoints and gating criteria:
- Gate 1 (Instrumentation complete) — must have request/response tracing, request-level latency histogram, success/failure flags, and prefix/KV cache hit metric present in telemetry.
  - Gate passes when: automated smoke (+50 synthetic requests) shows telemetry ingestion for 99% of traces.
- Gate 2 (SLO Eval in Staging) — test SLO rules in staging traffic replay for 72h with synthetic spikes.
  - Gate passes when: SLO rollout script flags neither continuous regressions nor data gaps; alert flapping < 5 events/day.
- Gate 3 (Canary to Production) — start with 1% traffic, then 5%, 20% for 24h each.
  - Gate passes when: P95 and error-rate within target for two consecutive 24h windows and error budget burn < threshold.

Representative SLOs (pilot definitions):
- Latency SLO (user-observed streaming): 99% of streaming responses must begin sending tokens within 800ms of request start for the primary region. (Violation = user-experienced stall).
- Success SLO (API): 99.5% of generation requests return a 2xx body with well-formed tokens (no truncated JSON) over a 30d rolling window.
- Embedding freshness SLO (batch): 95% of embedding jobs finish within expected SLA (batch window) during business hours.

Measurement and instrumentation details:
- Telemetry sources: request logs (edge + router), runtime traces (span-level for model forward pass), token emission histograms produced by serving runtime, prefix/KV cache hit counters.
- Aggregation: daily rollups in metrics store (Prometheus -> Cortex) and sliding-window windows exposed to Console.
- Data quality checks: ingestion-latency monitor, missing-tags detector, and a nightly job that validates P99 calculation against raw histograms.

Alerting & routing matrix:
- SLO-warning (burn rate > 2x expected for 1h) -> on-call SRE + platform slack channel (#platform-slo-warnings).
- SLO-breach (error budget burned 50% in 24h) -> SRE lead paging and product pager.
- Service-degraded (P95 latency > threshold OR tail latency spike) -> on-call SRE; escalate to runtime eng if CPU/GPU queues spike.
- Customer-impacting outage -> immediate bridge: on-call SRE + product + solutions + assigned engineer.

Runbooks (short form):
- High tail latency (P99): check queueing (GPU utilization, kernel stalls), verify KV cache hit rate, switch to lower-cost model variant or enable response-trimming on canary.
- Increased error rate: validate model inputs (schema drift), check upstream ingress errors (rate limit spikes), move traffic to fallback model version.
- Telemetry gaps: verify agent forwarders, check Prometheus push gateway, look for sampler misconfig.

Rollout cadence and timeline (example 10-week plan):
- Week 0-1: Kickoff; finalize SLO definitions and roles; instrumentation spec reviewed.
- Week 2-3: Instrumentation implementation (runtime + edge) + smoke tests.
- Week 4: Staging SLO replay and Gate 2 run.
- Week 5: Canary 1% -> 5% -> 20% with 24h observations.
- Week 6-7: Post-canary tuning and second pilot (embedding).
- Week 8-10: Harden runbooks, finalize dashboards, and run a tabletop incident sim.

Dependencies and risks:
- Dependency: metrics storage capacity — Cortex retention must support high-cardinality histograms for token latency. Mitigation: reduce cardinality and enable nightly aggregation.
- Dependency: app teams must add tagging to requests for customer tenancy; mitigation: feature flag with fallback to anonymous tag.
- Risk: alert fatigue from noisy SLO derivations. Mitigation: tune burn-rate thresholds, introduce suppression windows for known non-actionable spikes.

Communication plan:
- Weekly sync (30m) for the launch squad; agenda: instrumentation status, gate readiness, customer notes.
- Weekly update to Reliability Guild; short digest with metrics and open blockers.
- Beta customers: pre-signed emails and in-console notices for planned ramp windows.

Success criteria and acceptance:
- SLOs defined & measurable with >99% data coverage for requested metrics.
- Two pilot features complete canary-to-stable with runbooks used for at least one real incident recovery.
- Error budget burn rate reduced below threshold for 30d post-launch or documented mitigation path in place.

Open questions and decisions needed:
1) Do we adopt a single cross-service SLO baseline or per-feature SLOs? (Product + SRE decision by Nov 22).
2) What is the error-budget governance model for compounding degradations across small services? (proposal: nominate an error-budget steward per domain).
3) Which console visualization will be the canonical source for SLO status? (Platform to recommend by Gate 2).

Next actions (owner + due):
- Ava Chen: finalize Gate checklist and post in Confluence (due 2026-11-20).
- Marcus Li: land runtime histogram PR and instrumentation test (PR #84) (due 2026-11-29).
- Priya Rao: prototype dashboard wireframe and SLO tile (due 2026-12-06).
- Diego Martinez: recruit two beta customers and schedule tabletop (due 2026-12-10).

Appendix (short snippets):
- Example SLO math: rolling-30d window, target 99.5% success. Burn-rate calculation uses (observed bad / allowed bad) where allowed bad = (1 - SLO) * window_duration.
- Canary script checklist: traffic-shift automation, health checks, automatic rollback trigger on >2x burn rate or 3 consecutive 5m alerts.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a living document. The emphasis for this draft is on operational clarity and minimal gating friction for teams launching product features. Provide feedback inline in Confluence or ping me on #sre-runbook.

-- Ava
